## Successful retry

Query:

> Primary official sources only: for Symfony extension compilation and Laravel Octane or queue long-lived workers, which guarantees support compile-before-use, deterministic ordering, immutable snapshots, cache invalidation, and refresh at a request/job boundary? Separate exact documented behavior from architecture inference. Include direct source links.

Perplexity response, preserved verbatim as returned by the MCP transport:

```csv
"Property","Symfony extensions + compiler passes","Laravel Octane","Laravel queue:work"
"Compile before runtime use","Documented: extensions are processed during ContainerBuilder::compile(); compiler passes manipulate definitions before services are instantiated. Compiled container is then dumped/cached.","Not applicable as a comparable mechanism: Octane boots Laravel once and retains the application in memory. No documented “compile all extensions before use” contract beyond Laravel’s normal bootstrap.","Not applicable as a comparable mechanism: a worker boots the Laravel application and then processes jobs repeatedly. Job handle() dependencies are resolved by the container at processing time."
"Deterministic ordering","Documented and configurable: pass type defines phase; within a phase, higher integer priority runs earlier.","No general documented ordering guarantee for arbitrary app-level refresh/rebuild work between requests.","No general documented ordering guarantee for arbitrary refresh/rebuild work between jobs. Queue priority such as --queue=high,default is selection priority, not a deterministic global execution order."
"Immutable snapshot","Documented at DI-definition level: service definitions can only be modified before compilation; after compilation they cannot be manipulated. A dumped container is a concrete generated PHP artifact.","No: the same application instance is reused. Octane resets first-party framework state, but explicitly may not know how to reset your application’s global state.","No: long-lived worker process retains booted application state; jobs and static/process state must be treated as potentially persistent."
"Cache invalidation","Documented for ConfigCache in debug mode: tracked resources include config files, extensions, and compiler passes; timestamp changes make cache stale and cause rebuild. In non-debug mode, existing cached container is always used.","Documented reload mechanism: file changes are not reflected merely by browser refresh; octane:reload gracefully restarts application workers so subsequently served requests use newly loaded code. --watch restarts on watched changes for development.","Documented restart mechanism: workers do not notice code changes until restarted. queue:restart tells workers to exit gracefully after their current job; a process manager must start replacements. Restart signals are stored/polled through the configured cache."
"Refresh boundary","Framework lifecycle-dependent: Symfony gives a compile/cache boundary, but request-boundary adoption of a new build is not specified by DI docs as a cluster-wide atomic deployment primitive.","Documented: graceful reload makes newly deployed code loaded into memory for subsequent requests. It does not document an atomic all-worker cutover or a request-to-single-version consistency guarantee across multiple workers.","Documented: graceful restart occurs after the current job; polling happens on each job iteration. This is a job boundary for the exiting worker, not a global atomic fleet cutover."
```

## Capture boundary

The MCP response did not include its source-link list despite the query. The factual rows were
therefore checked separately against the official Symfony and Laravel documentation in
`P11-Q2-primary-sources.md`. The negative claim about fleet-wide atomic cutover remains an
architectural inference from the absence of such a guarantee, not a framework promise.
